title: Universal Game Quality
description: Minimum coherence and release coverage for any complete game blueprint.

items.title: Distinct player promise
items.guidance: The game has a recognizable identity and a concrete player fantasy.

items.title: Complete core loop
items.guidance: Moment-to-moment, session, and long-term loops reinforce each other.

items.title: Beginning-to-ending path
items.guidance: The opening, progression, final challenge, terminal states, ending, and postgame are explicit.

items.title: Bounded launch scope
items.guidance: Every launch entry is named and categorized as must, optional, or cut.

items.title: Responsive controls
items.guidance: Inputs, timing, feedback, remapping, and controller behavior are specified and testable.

items.title: Meaningful decisions
items.guidance: Important choices have understandable consequences and non-trivial trade-offs.

items.title: Readable feedback
items.guidance: Visual, animation, audio, UI, accessibility, and controller feedback communicate game state.

items.title: Understandable onboarding
items.guidance: Players learn the first useful verb and decision without developer intervention.

items.title: Accessible information and input
items.guidance: The blueprint covers remapping, text, color, motion, audio alternatives, and difficulty assistance as applicable.

items.title: Reliable save and recovery
items.guidance: Progress, interruption, failure recovery, and save compatibility are defined.

items.title: Performance and compatibility
items.guidance: Target frame rate, loading, platform, input, and stability budgets are verifiable.

items.title: Systemic and emotional payoff
items.guidance: Mechanics, content, presentation, progression, and ending support the same intended experience.
